Outlet: Yahoo Finance live blog, updated Fri, November 6, 2026 at 9:59 PM GMT
Stock market today: Nasdaq and S&P 500 rebound, Dow slips to cap bruising week for AI stocks

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.4%, closing at 51,285.73, down 237.33 points. The S&P 500 rose 0.3% to 7,376.86, gaining 23.13 points. The Nasdaq Composite gained more than 1%, reaching 24,579.42, up 264.43 points.

Despite Friday's recovery, the major indexes posted significant weekly losses. The S&P 500 experienced "its worst weekly performance since June". The VIX Volatility Index fell 9.01% to 25.64.

On Thursday, markets experienced a severe sell-off erasing approximately $3 trillion in market value. The primary catalyst was Democrats' midterm election victory, which raised investor concerns about potential regulations affecting data center construction and AI infrastructure spending.

Chip stocks rebounded Friday after suffering their worst day since March 2020. The PHLX Semiconductor Index rose 4% after plunging 12% Thursday. Nvidia gained 6%, AMD climbed 8%, and Intel jumped nearly 6%.

The Labor Department reported the US economy added 165,000 jobs in October, significantly exceeding economist expectations of approximately 65,000-70,000. The unemployment rate edged down to 4.1% from expectations of 4.2%.

Anthropic's expected IPO valuation potentially declined to between $1 trillion and $1.3 trillion from previous $2 trillion projections amid market volatility. Iren stock surged 20% on strong AI cloud revenue results. Airbnb stock jumped after reporting third-quarter earnings per share of $3.16, beating estimates of $2.85.
